Santander Posts Lower Profit After Increase in Loan-Loss Provisions
Banco Santander posted a decline in third-quarter net profit after the bank set aside more funds to cover loan losses.

The Spanish bank said Wednesday that it made a third-quarter net profit of 3.43 billion euros ($3.82 billion), down 2% compared with the same period last year. The result was hit by a 22% increase in net loan-loss provisions to 3.49 billion euros.

On an underlying basis, Santander's net profit jumped 19% to 3.85 billion euros, it said. Analysts had forecast the metric at 3.79 billion euros, according to consensus estimates provided by the bank.
Total operating income--the group's top-line figure--grew to 15.89 billion euros from 14.27 billion euros, against consensus expectations of 16.09 billion euros.

Both net interest income--the difference between what banks earn on loans and pay on deposits--and fees contributed to the top-line increase. Santander reported net interest income of 11.83 billion euros, up from 10.35 billion euros, with net fee income rising to 3.5 billion euros from 3.16 billion euros.
Santander reiterated its full-year guidance, saying it is comfortably on track to meet its targets.
